items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Sometimes, Earl Humphrey used to work with him.

ctx.x: How long has he been dead? How long has he been dead? My brother must be dead about, um.

You see, my belly, my belly, I'm saying. See, time passed up, but my belly been dead about 23 years. I think Bud died before him. That's why his niece was two years old when my belly died. My brother died, George. You remember my brother George? He was a psycho. He wasn't much a musician, but he was, you know, make out sometimes, you know. He'd take a chance anyway, you know. Just better work, too. Yeah, I was all them boys. Lee Collins and, um, Lee Collins and, uh, Kid Rene. Oh, Bud Appetite. They all used to go…
Did you play with Bud before he was with the Liberty Bell or after?

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: and little dad, Vincent, Turner Banja, Roy Evans on drums

ctx.x: George, can you tell, who else was in the band? Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. and little dad, Vincent, Turner Banja, Roy Evans on drums, Earl Hunter, myself on trombone, Lee Collins on trumpet, and with the addition of Buddy, maybe we had two trumpets for us. Yes.

And a seven-piece arch. Well, now in this story, it's slightly different from the story I've had before, because I've heard that you played with Buddy, or he played with you in George Orson's song. Then you had some kind of a, you know, Buddy didn't get on with Buddy or something, and you fired Buddy, and you got Lee Collins after Buddy left. No, I don't remember that.
